subject.title: Core hardening tracker: converge duplicated runtime invariants onto single owners

question: Which remaining canonical-owner seams should OpenClaw approve and sequence next, given their distinct runtime, plugin, session-storage, and compatibility boundaries?
rationale: Source inspection confirms real duplication, but this umbrella intentionally does not establish that every proposed owner boundary is correct; repository policy requires area-owner judgment for broad core, provider, and session architecture changes.

options.title: Sequence strongest seams
options.body: Approve one source-proven seam at a time, prioritizing active behavioral drift and requiring separate owner-boundary and runtime proof for each PR.

options.title: Hold as research backlog
options.body: Keep the tracker open without approving more implementation until the relevant area owner validates each proposed canonical boundary.

options.title: Split by ownership domain
options.body: Replace the umbrella with separate agents, gateway, sessions, and provider trackers before accepting further implementation work.

recommendation.title: Sequence strongest seams
recommendation.body: Approve one source-proven seam at a time, prioritizing active behavioral drift and requiring separate owner-boundary and runtime proof for each PR.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced or recently owns several central contracts implicated by the proposed changes, including subagent authority, run staleness, and the session accessor boundary.
